metadata.purpose: Drop source values while the predicate is truthy, then permanently open on its first falsy result.

cardinality.signature: skipWhile : (T! x Index! -> Boolean!) -> T* -> T*
conditions: The first predicate-failing value and all later source values are forwarded. There is no buffer of skipped values.
Cω-style markers count values only; errors, cancellation and source lifetime remain separate parts of the contract.

scope.parameters: Named predicate; safe-integer indices until the gate opens
scope.callbacks: One named synchronous predicate invocation per tested input; correlated return/throw is an input. No user function executes in a guard, reaction or generator.
scope.time: No clock, timer or scheduler is created. Sources supply time; equal timestamps retain explicit delivery order. A predicate call/outcome is one synchronous logical reaction.
scope.reentrancy: Non-reentrant reactions, with cancellation between resolved value reactions. Exact source teardown traces use post-setup delivery; synchronous native checks are separate.
exclusions: Arbitrary source/observer/predicate reentry, cancellation during a predicate call, and throwing observers/finalizers.
Index overflow beyond nonnegative safe integers; invalid public callback arguments and compile-time narrowing proofs.
A production predicate interpreter and guarantees that user functions are pure.

initialization.sourceSubscription: One source connection on subscription, even for skip(0); no value is emitted by initialization.

ownership.sharing: No sharing is introduced. Each subscription owns its count or predicate gate even when the producer is hot.
ownership.reset: A fresh subscription starts with fresh bookkeeping. Closed executions accept no more model events.

resources.owner: external binding; invocation generation is execution-local

dispatch.actionSemantics: Compute the next state and ordered actions once. Predicate outcome must resolve before any subsequent external event; actions are descriptions, not executed effects.
cancellationCheckpoints: Between resolved inputs: release the source without a downstream complete notification.

rules.explanation: A result subscription connects to the source and starts its own predicate index at zero. No predicate runs until a source value arrives.

actions: invoke the predicate once with the input and its zero-based index
rules.nextState: calling with retained input, invocation identity and advanced index
rules.explanation: While testing, each source value requests one predicate call with the original value and its zero-based index. The predicate belongs to the user; the operator controls when it is called.

rules.nextState: testing with the already advanced index
rules.explanation: A truthy predicate result drops the value and keeps the gate closed.

rules.nextState: permanently open; predicate no longer called
rules.explanation: The first falsy predicate result opens the gate and forwards that same value. Later values no longer invoke the predicate.

actions: forward the incoming value without invoking the predicate
rules.explanation: Once open, skipWhile forwards all subsequent values unchanged. The predicate is not called again, even for a later value that would have satisfied it.

actions: forward the thrown value unchanged as an error
rules.explanation: A predicate throw errors downstream and releases the source. The failing input is never emitted, including with inclusive takeWhile.
Source completion from Testing completes downstream and releases the source without another predicate call or value.
A source error from Testing is forwarded without calling the predicate, then releases the source.

actions: release the source without notifying downstream
rules.explanation: Cancellation from Testing releases the source and does not complete downstream.
Source completion from Open completes downstream and releases the source without another predicate call or value.
A source error from Open is forwarded without calling the predicate, then releases the source.
